t.3.66.1: The king of Vidarbha is the righteous-souled Bhīma, of fearsome valor. This lovely lady is his daughter, renowned as Damayantī.
t.3.66.2: There is a king of Niṣadha, Nala by name, the son of Vīrasena; this fair lady is the wife of that wise one of holy renown.
t.3.66.3: That lord of the earth, defeated at dice by his brother and robbed of his kingdom, went away together with Damayantī, and he has not been found anywhere since.
t.3.66.4: We, then, wander over this earth for the sake of Damayantī; and here is that young woman, found in your son's dwelling.
t.3.66.5: No human woman here is her equal in beauty. And between the brows of this dark lady there is an excellent birthmark, born with her and resembling a lotus, which I have noticed though it is now concealed.
t.3.66.7: Like the crescent of the moon on the first day of the lunar fortnight, dimmed and clouded, she does not shine brightly; yet her beauty is not lost, and her body, though covered with dirt and unadorned, still clearly shines like gold.
t.3.66.6: For this mark of hers, now covered with dirt like the moon veiled by a thin cloud, was fashioned by the Creator as a sign, for the sake of her splendor.
t.3.66.8: By this form and by this very mole I have recognized this young woman as the queen, as a hidden fire is known by its heat.
t.3.66.9: Bṛhadaśva said: Having heard those words of Sudeva, O lord of the people, Sunandā washed away the dirt that was covering the mole.
t.3.66.10: When the dirt had been wiped away, that mole of Damayantī's then shone brightly, like the moon in a cloudless sky.
t.3.66.11: On seeing the mole, O Bhārata, Sunandā and the queen mother, weeping, embraced her and stood so for a moment. Then, slowly shedding tears, the queen mother said this:
t.3.66.12: You are my sister's daughter, made known by this mole. Your mother and I, O lovely one, are daughters of the high-souled kṣatriya Sudāman, lord of the Daśārṇas.
t.3.66.13: She was given to King Bhīma, and I, in turn, to Vīrabāhu. But you I saw when you were newly born, among the Daśārṇas, in my father's house.
t.3.66.14: Just as your father's house is yours, so too is this one, O beautiful lady; for just as this sovereignty is mine, Damayantī, so is it yours as well.
t.3.66.15: With a joyful heart, O lord of the people, Damayantī greeted her, her mother's sister, and spoke these words.
t.3.66.16: Even while I was unrecognized, I have lived happily here, well provided with every desire and always protected by you.
t.3.66.17: Without doubt, my stay here would be happier than happiness itself; yet, mother, you should give me leave to go, for I have long been away from home.
t.3.66.18: For my two children, who were taken there, are living there as little boys, bereft of their father and of me as well, and stricken with grief; how, then, are they faring?
t.3.66.19: And if you wish to do anything pleasing for me here, I wish to go to the Vidarbhas; quickly order a carriage for me.
t.3.66.21: The queen mother, O best of the Bharatas, sent her off in a splendid carriage borne by men, well furnished with good food, drink and attire.
t.3.66.20: Saying only “Very well” to her, O king, the delighted sister of her mother then, with her son’s consent, had her escorted under the protection of a great army.
t.3.66.22: Then, before long, that lovely lady reached the Vidarbhas, and all her kinsfolk, overjoyed, received her with honour.
t.3.66.23: Having seen all her kinsmen in good health, and those two children, her mother and her father, and the whole company of her friends,
t.3.66.24: The illustrious and auspicious Damayantī worshipped the gods and the brāhmaṇas with the highest rites, O lord of the people.
t.3.66.25: And the king, delighted at the mere sight of his daughter, gratified Sudeva with a thousand cows, a village, and wealth.
t.3.66.26: Having spent the night there in her father's house, the beautiful lady, now rested, spoke these words to her mother, O king.
